Application Materials.content:
- Identification Document: Singapore Citizen: a copy of NRIC; Singapore Permanent Resident: a copy of NRIC AND re-entry permit; Foreigner: a copy of passport personal particulars page.
- Two Referees: Two different referees are required. Please indicate the details of two referees in the online application form, including name, designation and email. The referee will receive a recommendation email from SMU once the LLM application is submitted. Where possible, at least one of the recommendations should be from someone who has taught the applicant or supervised applicant's work in university studies. If applicant has left school for a long time and is unable to submit academic references, please provide 2 referees from people who are familiar with applicant's performance, such as employers/colleagues/clients etc. The contents of the recommendation are confidential.
- Degree Certificate: The copy of the degree certificate(s) certified by the issuing institution or a Notary Public/Commissioner of Oath. The bachelor's degree certificate is compulsory. Combine all degree certificates into one PDF file.
- Transcript: The copy of the official transcript(s) certified by the issuing institution or a Notary Public/Commissioner of Oath. The undergraduate transcript is compulsory. Combine all official transcript in one PDF file.
- CV: A concise resume that provides chronological information about your educational background, work experiences and accomplishments. Up to two (2) A4 pages.
- Statement of Purpose: All applicants are required to submit a detailed personal statement based on the questions in the online application form. Maximum 600 words to each answer.
- Other Supporting Documents: If any additional significant supporting documents, please send them to smullm@smu.edu.sg with the applicant’s full name and application reference number by the application deadline. Kindly combine all documents into a single PDF file, with a maximum length of six A4 pages. No additional supporting documents will be accepted after the application deadline.

Interview Requirements.content:
| **Event** | **Date** |
| --- | --- |
| Admission Interviews | **December 2025 onwards** |
Shortlisted applicants will be required to take a LLM written test and participate in an interview online.
- Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an admission interview, which will be held individually (1 candidate to 1 faculty).
- The interview will be conducted via Zoom meeting.
- The LLM programme office will contact shortlisted candidates via email to register for the interview. Once the registration is confirmed, candidates will receive a confirmation email with a zoom link. Reminder emails are available near the interview date.
- Each interview session is around 15mins. No legal knowledge is compulsory.
- After the interview, LLM programme office will update application status via email within 2 weeks in general.

Application Deadlines.content: The application for 2026 intake is closed.

| Track | Entry Requirements |

GRE GMAT Requirements.content: GRE/GMAT, LSAT/LNAT or SMU Admission Test (SMUAT) is not required to the LLM application. **DO NOT pay the** _**'Optional Fee: 1st Attempt for SMU Admission Test (S$125)',**_ which is not required to the LLM programme.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Proof of English language proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS) is required for all international applicants except those from English-medium institutions in _Australia, Canada, Hong Kong, Ireland, New Zealand, Philippines, United Kingdom and the United States_. The minimum English proficiency test requirement is as follows:
- IELTS (Academic): **Overall Band of 6.5**
- TOEFL (Paper Based Test or Internet Based Test): **90**
- From 21 January 2026, TOEFL introduces a new score scale from 1 to 6 in increments of 0.5. The minimum TOEFL score under the new scale is: TOEFL (Paper Based Test or Internet Based Test): **Overall Band of 4.5**
Test scores are valid for **two (2) years** from the test date and applicants should ensure their scores remain valid at the beginning of the application period for the LL.M. track applied for. Apart from the above tests, others such as TOEFL Institutional Testing Program (ITP), TOEFL MyBest Scores or Duolingo English Test are not accepted. For the English proficiency test requirements of the Dual LLM in Commercial Law programme, please refer to [QMUL's website](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/coursefinder/courses/commercial-law-dual-llm-london-and-singapore-llm/) directly. Applicants intending to take the proficiency test are advised to schedule their test sufficiently early to ensure that their score reports are available before the closing date for the submission of supporting documents. Only official score reports are accepted.

Program Overview.content:
Singapore, one of the world’s most cosmopolitan cities, has emerged as Asia’s legal and financial hub. As an integral part of the central business district where leading law firms and banks are located, Singapore Management University (SMU) is at the forefront of legal education.
The SMU LLM programme is carefully designed to expand your legal knowledge in classic and novel areas of the law, while simultaneously equipping you with the skills-sets essential to render on-point advice on cross-border transactions or deliver high-quality adjudication and judicial administration results.
Our professors who have gained insight from diverse work experiences will engage you with their interdisciplinary knowledge. Small class sizes allow for highly interactive seminars that also provide a challenging yet collegial learning environment.
The School of Law’s active engagement with the legal community, as well as our strong alumni network and the Career Services team, immensely benefit students’ future careers. The SMU LLM will offer you an unparalleled opportunity for advanced legal education in Singapore and Asia.

Curriculum.content:
| Track | Curriculum / structure |
| --- | --- |
| [Judicial Studies Track](https://law.smu.edu.sg/llm/curriculum/judicial-studies-track) | Academic year: August to April (**1 yr full-time / 2 yrs extended duration**). No. of credit units: **9.5 credit units (CUs)**, comprising: 3 CUs common core modules; 3 CUs track core modules; 2 CUs electives; 1 CU PGPD workshops; 0.5 CU internship (optional for experienced candidates). |
| [Cross-Border Business and Finance Law in Asia Track](https://law.smu.edu.sg/llm/curriculum/cross-border-business-and-finance-law-asia) | Academic year: August to April (**1 yr full-time / 2 yrs part-time**). The Part-time LL.M. is a two-year programme. Part-time students attend the same classes as full-time students, but complete the programme over a longer duration with greater flexibility in their course schedule. LL.M. classes are conducted on weekdays only, with modules scheduled during either the daytime or the evening. There are no weekend classes. The Programme Office will endeavour to offer evening classes where possible, but this cannot be guaranteed. |
| [Law and Technology Track](https://law.smu.edu.sg/llm/curriculum/law-and-technology-track) | Academic year: January to April the following year (**16 months full-time**). |
| [Dual LLM in Commercial Law (Singapore & London) Track](https://law.smu.edu.sg/llm/curriculum/dual-llm-commercial-law-singapore-london-track) | No. of credit units: **7.5 SMU credit units + 135 QMUL credits**. |
Additional curriculum links: [Programme Structure](https://law.smu.edu.sg/llm/curriculum/programme-structure), [Courses Offered](https://law.smu.edu.sg/llm/curriculum/courses-offered).

Cost of Attendance.content:
Singapore has one of the highest cost of living in South East Asia. These estimates do not include tuition fees and travel expenses from your home country to Singapore. An international student in Singapore spends, on average, about S$1,000 to S$3,000 a month on living expenses. This amount will vary depending on lifestyle and course of study.
| Item | Cost per Month (SGD) | Comments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accommodation | $500 - $2000 | Rental varies with geographical area, type of accommodation, demand, facilities provided & the number of people sharing, etc |
| Utilities (including water and electricity) | $40 - $100 | |
| Food | $300 - $500 | Based on $10-$15 per day for 3 meals at a foodcourt. |
| Transportation | $100 | Depends on the distance and mode of transport. |
| Telecommunications | $50 | Varies with usage and promotional packages subscribed for telephone services, mobile services and internet access services. |
| Books & Stationery | From $100/term | Booklink at the SMU concourse stocks almost all the required textbooks. |
| Personal Expenses | $100 - $300 | Varies with the individual. Could include expenses on clothes, toiletries, entertainment, haircut, miscellaneous. |
| Medical Insurance | | As a SMU student, you are automatically entitled to SMU Medical Insurance Coverage scheme that covers your basic medical treatment and consultation. |

Financial Aid.content:
The Singapore Management University (SMU) reserves the right to amend the discount schemes for new incoming cohorts when required. Discounts will not be awarded in conjunction with other ongoing discount schemes; discount and scholarship are not stackable. Should a student qualify for more than one discount, only the higher discount amount will be applicable.
- **SMU Alumni:** S$8,000 discount off total tuition fees from 2025 intake onwards.
- **Singapore Citizens/ Permanent Residents Discount:** S$5,000 discount off total tuition fees from 2025 intake onwards.
- **SMU LLM Scholarship:** Up to four bond-free scholarships per academic year. Each scholarship has an annual value of S$10,000, disbursed in 2 equal installments of $5,000 to offset tuition fees in Term 1 and Term 2. Open to all LLM applicants, full-time and part-time, who are offered a place in the programme; applicants must not be recipients of other scholarship or sponsorship. Application via an application form is required once applicants accept the offer.
- **ASEAN Nationals Discount:** From 2025 intake onward, a S$3,000 discount off total tuition fees is granted to students from ASEAN nations.
- **SMU PG ASEAN Scholarship:** The scholarship co-funds outstanding individuals in pursuit of the SMU LLM / Dual LLM programme. It has a value of $10,000 and offers financial support towards tuition fees, living allowances and the purchase of textbooks. No bond is required. Open to citizens of ASEAN member and observer nations; at least "Very Good" admissions interview and essay scores; must not be a recipient of other scholarship or sponsorship; special consideration may be given to students with financial needs. No application is required; eligible ASEAN candidates will automatically be considered.
- **SkillsFuture:** SkillsFuture funding for Singapore Citizens is available; Singapore Citizens aged 40 years and above can claim SkillsFuture Credit (Base Tier) and $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-career Tier). This credit is intended to offset out-of-pocket tuition fees, starting from Academic Year 2024/25 intake, commencing on or after 1 May 2024. SkillsFuture Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy up to 90% of course fees is not applied to the SMU LLM programme.
- **Post Secondary Education Account (PSEA):** Singapore Citizens with eligible Post Secondary Education Account may utilize balance funds for tuition fees.
- **Lee Kuan Yew Scholarship:** Applicants must be Singapore citizens and will be assessed holistically, including track record of leadership and achievement and potential to contribute to and benefit Singapore and society.
- **Jones Day Master of Laws in Judicial Studies Scholarship:** Up to four scholarships for outstanding candidates enrolled in LLM (Judicial Studies). Candidates must have been accepted into the LLM (Judicial Studies), not be a Singapore citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident, hold an LLB or JD from a reputable law school, demonstrate strong leadership aspirations and abilities, and have strong professional references. Two Jones Day (Judicial Studies) Scholarships for international candidates of $40,000 each; bond-free. Candidates cannot simultaneously hold any other scholarships.
- **Jones Day Master of Laws Annual Top Scholar Award (for Judicial Studies):** The best performing graduate of the LLM in Judicial Studies will receive the Jones Day Top Scholar Award. One award per annum, with a monetary value of S$10,000.
- **Lee Kong Chian Master of Laws in Judicial Studies Scholarship:** Up to six annual scholarships for outstanding candidates enrolled in LLM (Judicial Studies), intended to offset tuition fees and cannot be used to defray living expenses. Up to 4 Singapore citizens or permanent residents and up to 2 international candidates. Candidates must have been accepted into the LLM (Judicial Studies), hold an LLB or JD from a reputable law school, demonstrate strong leadership aspirations and abilities, and have strong professional references; special consideration may be given to candidates who demonstrate financial need, in particular those from non-OECD countries. Four scholarships for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents of $20,000 each; two scholarships for international candidates of $40,000 each; bond-free. Candidates cannot simultaneously hold any other scholarships.

Multiple Applications.content:
Applicants can apply for **up to three master programmes in a single online form**. Those interested in **Master of Laws (LLM)** and **Juris Doctor (JD)** may apply for both together.
SMU LLM has three available tracks. Applicants must indicate **one track** in the online application form, and pursue only that track throughout LLM studies. Enrolled students may request to switch track prior to the commencement of the LLM programme, subject to the programme director’s approval.
If an applicant is also applying for other programmes in the same application form, they should follow the requirements specified for those additional programmes.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
- SMU PG ASEAN Scholarship: Applicants must matriculate into the SMU PG programme for which the scholarship has been awarded with. As the scholarship offered is only valid for this FY, matriculated students who defer their studies will not be able to carry forward their scholarships.
- Jones Day Master of Laws in Judicial Studies Scholarship: Matriculated candidates who opt to defer their admission offer or studies will not be able to carry forward the scholarships.
- Lee Kong Chian Master of Laws in Judicial Studies Scholarship: Matriculated candidates who opt to defer their admission offer or studies will not be able to carry forward the scholarships.

Conditional Admission Policy.content: Those completing their first degree by **early July of the year of admission** may apply using their latest provisonal transcript. Students will be asked to submit their final transcript and graduate certificate letter/degree scroll later if they are offered a place in the programme.
